pages.text: Mathematics starts from almost nothing: a few rules of logic, the empty set, and counting.

$(thing)Primes$(): the $(item)Sieve of Eratosthenes$() crosses out the multiples of each prime and keeps what is left, about N / ln N numbers up to N. Set its limit high enough for the recipe, and a wheel to skip the small primes: less work is faster. It makes $(item)Prime Shards$() from Natural Number Lattices, or from Axiom Stone.

$(thing)Cardinality$(): zero is the empty set and one is the set holding it. The Formal Proof Assistant makes $(item)Zero$() and $(item)Unity$(), two of the five constants of Euler's identity. Physics uses them too: Zero presses a Casimir Plate with half the neutronium, Unity normalises a qubit with half the parts.
$(thing)Proof by Induction$(): a $(item)Proof Certificate$() filed with a multiblock (use it on the controller; up to four) catches one containment failure each, and nothing is released.
$(thing)Combinatorics$(): the Peano Engine counts $(item)Microstate Tallies$(), Boltzmann's W, and the Maxwell Demon Sorter builds its chip from them with far less.
